intent: Hold the iteration 7 geometry fixed (outer sensors at x = ±0.03, y = 0.04, 15 mm spacing, 0.016 footprint, 0.18 m by 0.12 m body, 0.8 kg, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheel radius). The best race so far (160.5) came from this layout, so the next race isolates the controller change. Expected: a score at or near 160, with oval completions holding and slalom rms_error at or below 0.031 with the new damping. If the score drops well below 160 and the oval completions fall, the damping change is the cause, not the geometry.
learning: Iteration 7 showed the outer reach at ±0.03 beats ±0.036 under the same damping: the score rose from 97.7 to 160.5, the oval finished 2 of 20 trials (mean progress 0.81), and the slalom rms returned toward the iteration 4 level. The wider ±0.036 reach was costing slalom centring rather than helping. The geometry now looks settled. The remaining levers are the controller damping and, if slalom line loss persists, wheel_track 0.14 as a single-variable test. Ask the Integrator whether the kd change to 0.35 keeps oval completions and whether slalom line_loss_events fall below 1.
rationale:
Iteration 7 (outer sensors at x = ±0.03, 15 mm spacing, y = 0.04, 0.016 footprint, 0.18 m / 0.8 kg body, 0.12 m track) is the best race so far at 160.5, up from 97.7 in iteration 6. The gain is concentrated on the oval, where 2 of 20 trials finished and mean progress rose to 0.81. That is the 500-point completion term, so it dominates the score.

The comparison is clean. Iterations 6 and 7 share the same controller (kd 0.25, as the Integrator's feedback describes) and differ only in outer reach (±0.036 vs ±0.03). Pulling the outer pair back to ±0.03 gave a score of 160.5 against 97.7. The slalom rms that rose to 0.0333 at ±0.036 is therefore tied to the wider reach, not only to the damping. The Integrator's feedback was written against the iteration 5 geometry and does not account for iteration 7's result, so I do not follow its request to revert to ±0.036.

The body (0.18 m, 0.8 kg) stays, because iteration 2 showed the lighter body cost s-bend progress. The footprint (0.016) and y = 0.04 row stay, because iterations 3 to 5 showed them neutral to slightly positive.

I hold the iteration 7 geometry unchanged. This lets the Integrator's damping change (kd, which they plan to raise to 0.35) be read against a fixed platform that has the best evidence. Changing wheel_track in the same race would confound that reading, so I leave it for a later iteration if slalom line loss persists. Expected result: a score at or near 160 if the controller holds, with oval completion still the main driver. If the score falls well below 160, the kd change is the likely cause rather than the geometry.
